memory_update.text: US-listed pure-play merchant suppliers of high-end sub-100nm barium titanate powder appear scarce; key powder names found in evidence are mostly Japan/China listings or private entities such as Ferro/Vibrantz.

VSH and KN are the best current US-listed underfollowed discovery-lane candidates, but both are MLCC/ceramic capacitor product hypotheses rather than confirmed high-end BaTiO3 powder chokepoint beneficiaries.
MRAAY and TTDKY should be retained as reference leaders for AI-server MLCC demand validation, not as underfollowed alpha candidates.
Next layer should separately map non-US direct powder suppliers: Sakai Chemical, Nippon Chemical Industrial, Fuji Titanium, Shandong Sinocera, and private Vibrantz/Ferro.

Sakai Chemical / SACIF should be promoted to a focused Layer 2 verification target for AI-server MLCC upstream dielectric powder exposure, with emphasis on BaTiO3 share, nano-hydrothermal capability, capacity, and customer evidence.

Nippon Chemical Industrial / NPNHF is a speculative shadow candidate due to official barium-carbonate-to-BaTiO3-for-MLCC product evidence, but US OTC ticker/liquidity and revenue materiality must be verified before inclusion in a stronger universe.

The strongest current fact pattern is downstream demand pull: Murata materials and industry reports support rising AI-server MLCC intensity; upstream powder tightness remains a hypothesis requiring supplier-level evidence.
US-listed pure-play access to high-end BaTiO3 dielectric powder appears limited; the practical US-accessible universe may rely on OTC Japanese listings plus reference ADRs for MLCC makers.

For the AI server MLCC dielectric-powder node, direct public-market exposure appears stronger in Japan-listed suppliers such as Sakai Chemical and Nippon Chemical Industrial than in clean US-listed names.
MTRN should enter the US-listed underfollowed watchlist as a hypothesis-only BaTiO3 specialty-materials candidate; survival requires proof of MLCC-grade commercial sales or capacitor-maker customers.
VSH is a second-order MLCC-component proxy, not an upstream dielectric-powder supplier; keep only if evidence appears for AI-server-qualified MLCC orders, pricing, or capacity tightness.
CBT is a stale-asset trail: historical Cabot barium titanate ceramics exposure exists, but the current product/business status must be confirmed before use in later Serenity layers.

The purest high-end BaTiO3 dielectric-powder suppliers for AI-server MLCCs appear to be non-US listed or private; US-listed exposure is mostly downstream MLCC makers, OTC ADRs, or adjacent passive-component suppliers.

Sakai Chemical 4078.JP should remain the key non-US upstream reference for future non-US universe expansion, but it should not be inserted into a US-listed candidate list unless a verifiable US-traded ordinary/ADR instrument is found.

For US-listed candidates, the correct falsification test is not simply MLCC exposure; it is evidence of high-capacitance/thin-layer MLCC demand, AI-server qualification, pricing power, capacity tightness, or dielectric-powder procurement constraints.

Vishay is the best-fit US-listed underfollowed candidate found in this pass, but its direct link to AI-server-grade thin-layer MLCCs and sub-100nm BaTiO3 powder is weak and must be treated as a hypothesis until product mix and customer exposure are verified.

The most direct public exposure is mostly via non-US companies with US OTC ADR access or via US-listed specialty passive-component makers that consume MLCC ceramic dielectrics rather than produce merchant BaTiO3 powder. Reference lane anchors are Murata and TDK because they are obvious MLCC leaders with visible AI/data-center MLCC relevance. Underfollowed lane candidates are Vishay and Knowles: both are US-listed, smaller than the Japanese reference leaders, and make MLCC/ceramic capacitor products, but their exposure to sub-100nm BaTiO3 powder tightness is an inference that needs customer, sourcing, margin, and product-mix verification. The cleanest underfollowed lane is not US domestic: it is Japan-listed specialty chemicals accessible through OTC foreign ordinary shares/ADRs where available. Reference names such as Murata and TDK help validate demand and customer pull, but the discovery focus is upstream barium titanate and barium-carbonate suppliers, especially Sakai Chemical and Nippon Chemical Industrial. Evidence is still early: AI-server MLCC demand is visible in Murata/industry commentary, while supplier-specific AI-server revenue exposure needs verification through segment filings, capacity disclosures, customer commentary, and pricing data.
